# sherpa-node-stage

One STAGE of a workflow: a column across a [sherpa-layout-canvas](sherpa-layout-canvas.md), in its `columns` slot. Its BAR runs along the canvas's top with its name; its BAND, faint in its colour, runs down the view. Its host writes where it stands and how wide (data-x, data-w, plane px): it pans and zooms across, never down. On a hover its bar shows More: Edit and Remove. The last stage also shows Add stage, and a More of its own: Arrange stages. Arranging, a drag on the bar, or an arrow key there, reports how far: its host orders the stages. Will, 2026-11-10

## When to use it

For the stages of a workflow on a `sherpa-layout-canvas`: one column each, in its `columns` slot, its bar along the top with its name and its band down the view. Its host writes where it stands and how wide (`data-x`, `data-w`, plane px), its colour, and `data-removable` while it is not the only one; More reports `stage-menu-select` (Edit, Remove). The last (`data-last`) shows Add stage (`stage-add`) and Arrange stages (`stage-arrange`). Arranging (`data-editing`), a drag on the bar reports `stage-drag`, and an arrow key `stage-step`; its host orders the stages. For nodes that belong together anywhere on the canvas, use `sherpa-node-frame`.

## Example

```html
<sherpa-layout-canvas style="inline-size: 900px; block-size: 360px"><sherpa-node-stage slot="columns" data-heading="Intake" data-description="Where the rows come in" data-colour="#3b4ccd" data-x="40" data-w="360" data-removable></sherpa-node-stage><sherpa-node-stage slot="columns" data-heading="Decide" data-x="416" data-w="320" data-removable data-last></sherpa-node-stage><sherpa-node data-heading="Source" data-icon="storage" data-x="88" data-y="96" data-output-socket="object"></sherpa-node></sherpa-layout-canvas>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-colour` | text |  | a CSS colour its bar and band wear; none, the default look |
| `data-description` | text |  | its line: its bar's tip, under the name |
| `data-editing` | boolean |  | arranging the stages: the bar is a handle, and More, Add stage and Arrange stages hide. The HOST writes it |
| `data-heading` | text | `Stage` | its name, on its bar (default Stage) |
| `data-last` | boolean |  | the last stage: Add stage and Arrange stages show after its bar |
| `data-locked` | boolean |  | the host is read only: no More, no Add stage |
| `data-removable` | boolean |  | More offers Remove: it is not the only stage. The HOST writes it |
| `data-w` | number | `320` | its width, in plane px |
| `data-x` | number | `0` | its left edge, in plane px |

## Events

Each one bubbles.

| Event | Detail | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `stage-menu-select` | `{ action: string }` | More's Edit or Remove was picked. |
| `stage-add` |  | Add stage was pressed: its host adds a stage after the last |
| `stage-arrange` |  | Arrange stages was picked: its host starts arranging |
| `stage-drag` | `{ dx: number; phase: 'cancel' \| 'end' \| 'move' }` | Arranging, its bar was dragged. |
| `stage-step` | `{ by: number }` | Arranging, an arrow key on its bar. |

## Parts

Style these from outside with `::part()`:

`add`, `band`, `bar`, `column`, `end`, `grip`, `heading`, `more`, `stages`, `swatch`, `tip`
